HEADLINE: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in north-east Nigeria

CORE FACTS
- Unknown gunmen raided the remote village of Binnari, Karim Lamido area, Taraba state, north-eastern Nigeria, killing at least 10 people, looting shops and setting houses ablaze, police say.
- The gunmen swooped on the village mounted on motorcycles just after midday Muslim prayers on Friday, in a rampage that went on for up to four hours.
- Police recovered 10 bodies with gunshot wounds after officers responded to a distress call. The attackers had fled by the time police arrived.
- No claim of responsibility is reported. The attackers are described only as "unknown gunmen".

THREE-WAY CASUALTY CONFLICT (do not average)
- POLICE: at least 10 killed (10 bodies recovered with gunshot wounds).
- EYEWITNESSES/SURVIVORS: at least 20 dead. Survivors who spoke to AFP said they had counted at least 20 dead.
- AMNESTY INTERNATIONAL: up to 50 dead. Amnesty's Nigeria director Isa Sanusi told BBC News on Saturday the NGO had spoken to bereaved families who said up to 50 people had died, adding: "The initial funeral had 37 people."

NAMED QUOTES
- Assistant Superintendent of Police Victor Mshelizah: "We were able to disperse the unknown gunmen though there was no casualty on their side and ours because the terrain is difficult and they're used to the terrain." He said officers were still searching the bush for people who might have been killed or wounded and warned the death toll could still rise.
- Community leader Malam Abubakar Saifullahi told AFP the attackers arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece: "They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions. They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack."
- Binnari resident Isiyaku Musa: "People were running in different directions to escape the attack. Nobody knew where it was safe to go."
- Survivor Sa'idu Nuhu said some people were still missing.
- Amnesty's Isa Sanusi called for an impartial investigation, accusing the authorities of leaving rural communities "at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity" [sic, as published].

SECOND SOURCE: Al Jazeera, "Gunmen kill at least 10 people in eastern Nigeria, police say", 24 Oct 2026 — carries the police figure of at least 10 and the ~50 motorcycles detail. Note Al Jazeera describes the location as "eastern Nigeria" where the BBC says "north-east".
